sections.content: CREATE TABLE defines structure: column names, data types (INT, VARCHAR, DATE, BOOLEAN, DECIMAL), constraints (PRIMARY KEY, NOT NULL, UNIQUE, DEFAULT).
PRIMARY KEY uniquely identifies each row; foreign keys link tables. Choose types carefully — altering types later is painful.
Key points: VARCHAR(n) for variable text, DECIMAL for money (never FLOAT), and every table should have a primary key.
Try this variation — change a value, predict the output, then run it:
sections.codeExample:
CREATE TABLE users (
    id INT PRIMARY KEY,
    name VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL,
    email VARCHAR(100) UNIQUE,
    created_at DATE DEFAULT CURRENT_DATE
);
-- experiment: modify a value above and predict the new output
